records.name_note: Sources split on which common name to lead with. NC State's dedicated page leads with Flowering Fern: its Common Name(s) list gives Flowering Fern then Royal Fern, and its Description opens 'Flowering fern is an herbaceous perennial fern with an arching habit.' The other two dedicated species pages lead with royal fern: MoBot's Common Name row reads 'Common Name: royal fern,' and RHS shows 'royal fern' as the common name beneath the botanical name, with royal fern absent from its 'Other common names' list. On related taxa: NC State's 'Osmunda regalis is often confused with:' module lists three species — Athyrium niponicum, Comptonia peregrina and Osmunda spectabilis — and its 'Native alternative(s) for Osmunda regalis:' module lists Osmunda spectabilis and Osmundastrum cinnamomeum. NC State thus treats O. spectabilis, the American segregate, as both a commonly-confused look-alike and a native alternative; no source treats it as a synonym of O. regalis. Distinct from Osmundastrum cinnamomeum (Cinnamon Fern), already in this catalog.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: none of the three admissible sources consulted (NC State, RHS, MoBot) carry a toxicity/poison section for Osmunda regalis at all — NC State's page has no Poison field, and neither RHS nor MoBot's pages mention toxicity to cats, dogs, or any other animal.

is_houseplant is set false on the strength of all three sources' framing this exclusively as an outdoor wet-site/landscape fern (naturalized areas, rain gardens, water gardens, woodland, riparian sites); no source discusses indoor container culture.

chill_damage_f left null: no source states a numeric damage-onset temperature. NC State gives only a USDA hardiness zone range (3a-10b) and RHS/MoBot give only zone ratings, which per instructions cannot be converted into a chill-damage figure.
day/night F min/max and humidity fields left null: no admissible source gives explicit day/night temperature ranges or humidity percentages for this species.

light_fc_min, light_fc_good, and direct_sun_hours_max left null: no source gives foot-candle figures, and the only hour figures present (NC State's '6 or more hours' for Full sun and '2-6 hours' for Partial Shade) are the site-wide light-category legend text, not species-specific prose, so they cannot be used per the sourcing rules.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes full_sun. NC State's Light tags and RHS's Position field both carry a bare 'Full sun' tag, but MoBot's structured Sun field is 'Part shade to full shade' and MoBot's Culture text says 'Full sun exposure is not recommended for the hot St. Louis summers.'; NC State and RHS only allow full sun under a cool-summer / constant-moisture condition. part_shade and full_shade are carried.

soil_drainage is set to moisture_retentive on NC State's structured Soil Drainage field (Frequent Standing Water, Moist, Occasionally Wet, with no Good Drainage or dry value), cited first per the drainage rule, corroborated by RHS's Cultivation sentence 'Useful for very wet sites.' and MoBot's Uses sentence 'Excellent selection for wet areas along ponds, streams, water gardens or in bogs.' This is in some tension with RHS's structured Moisture field, which also offers 'Moist but well-drained' (a moderate reading) as an accepted option alongside 'Poorly-drained'; no source frames a hard, unconditional wet-soil requirement in prose (NC State and MoBot both use 'prefers'/'best grown', not 'requires').

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: RHS's structured pH field accepts Acid, Alkaline, and Neutral soils (i.e., effectively unrestricted), and NC State has no Soil pH band field on this species page at all, so no ceiling or floor can be set.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, and water_dormant_days_est left null: this is an in-ground landscape perennial and no source frames watering in terms of a dry-down target, check depth, or day-interval schedule.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength left null: none of the three admissible sources discuss fertilizing this species.

soil_base is set to garden_bed as the best fit among the strict enum options, inferred from NC State's Landscape Location/Landscape Theme fields (naturalized area, woodland, riparian, rain garden, water garden) describing in-ground landscape placement; no source uses a 'soil_base' or potting-mix vocabulary directly, since this is not treated as a container/houseplant species by any source.

records.name_note: This species is sometimes filed under the segregate genus name Lorinseria areolata. NC State's dedicated species page treats Woodwardia areolata as the accepted name (its rendered H1 is the binomial 'Woodwardia areolata') and files 'Blechnum angustifolium' and 'Lorinseria areolata' under its 'Previously known as:' list rather than as separate species. Its single Common Name(s) entry is 'Netted Chain Fern', and Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated page (kempercode v200) carries the same lead name: its Common Name field reads 'netted chain fern' and its prose opens 'Woodwardia areolata, commonly called netted chain fern'. The catalog's first Woodwardia.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: NC State's dedicated Woodwardia areolata page carries no Poison field, MoBot's dedicated page (checked at landing) carries no toxicity statement, and no other admissible source addressed toxicity for this species.

chill_damage_f and cool_rest_note left null: no admissible source states a numeric damage-onset temperature; NC State only gives a USDA hardiness-zone range (3a-9b), which is a survival/hardiness rating, not an onset temperature.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_pct_min/max, and light_fc_min/good left null: no admissible source gives numeric day/night temperature, humidity percentage, or footcandle light figures for this species.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the hour ranges in NC State's Light values (e.g. 'Deep shade (Less than 2 hours to no direct sunlight)') are the toolbox's site-wide category definitions, repeated identically on every plant page, not a species-specific figure for Woodwardia areolata, so per the sourcing rules they cannot set this field.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes full_sun: NC State's prose that the fern 'will take a considerable amount of sun as long as soils are kept consistently moist' is a conditional tolerance aside, not an unconditional statement, so full_sun was not added.

soil_drainage moisture_retentive rests on NC State's structured Soil Drainage field (Frequent Standing Water, Moist, Occasionally Wet -- no Good Drainage value, so not the moderate Good Drainage + Moist pair), its cultivation prose ('consistently moist to wet'), its Resistance To Challenges value Wet Soil, and MoBot's Problems sentence 'Needs consistently moist soils.' The research record had nulled the field on a supposed disagreement with UGA's 'Wet to moderately dry soils'; that text is the content of UGA's Habitat field ('Habitat: Wet to moderately dry soils. Also found in acidic soils of swampy woods, along streams, or near wet, shaded rocks.'), a description of where the fern grows in the wild rather than a cultivation drainage recommendation, and UGA's own cultivation sentence ('It is a good choice for a moist, partially shaded garden.') agrees with NC State. Restored at landing on the audit's reasoning.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State's Soil pH field reads 'Acid (<6.0)', an open-ended band with no stated floor, and RHS (which could otherwise supply a closed pH range or contradict an alkaline ceiling) does not carry a page for this species, so no numeric bound could be set.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength left null: no admissible source addressed fertilizing this species.
humidity_need left null: no admissible source states a humidity requirement for this outdoor landscape fern.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, and water_estimate_basis left null: this is an in-ground landscape/native perennial fern and no source frames its watering in dry-down, depth-check, or day-interval terms.

RHS (www.rhs.org.uk) does not carry a plant page for Woodwardia areolata or Lorinseria areolata -- a site search returned no matching result -- so RHS could not corroborate scientific_name_accepted, hardiness rating, or any cultivation field.

Clemson HGIC (hgic.clemson.edu), UF/IFAS (edis.ifas.ufl.edu / ask.ifas.ufl.edu), Penn State Extension (extension.psu.edu), and University of Maryland Extension (extension.umd.edu) returned no dedicated or species-specific content for Woodwardia areolata / netted chain fern in the searches performed, so none contributed fields.

Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder was not consulted during research (the record reported a TLS certificate-chain failure that the audit could not reproduce). Re-checked at landing: MoBot carries a dedicated Woodwardia areolata page (kempercode v200), cited here for the common name, sun, water and drainage fields; its structured fields read 'Sun: Part shade to full shade' and 'Water: Medium to wet', its Culture paragraph reads 'Easily grown in organically rich, medium to wet, well-drained soils in part shade to full shade.', and its Problems section states 'Needs consistently moist soils.' MoBot's Family field reads Blechnaceae where NC State's Description says 'spleenwort family (Aspleniaceae)'; that family disagreement bears on no field in this record.

is_houseplant false rests on NC State's Plant Type field (Fern, Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant), its USDA Plant Hardiness Zone range (3a-9b) and its Description ('a deciduous herbaceous perennial ... native to the eastern United States and Nova Scotia'); no admissible source frames it as a houseplant one way or the other.

UGA Extension's fern guide is a multi-species publication (covers many Georgia native ferns), so per the single-species-page rule it was used only to corroborate facts already anchored on NC State's dedicated species page, never as the primary source for common_name or name authority.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name is primary. RHS's dedicated single-species page for Thelypteris palustris leads with "marsh fern" as its common name/subtitle. NC State Extension's dedicated page covers Thelypteris palustris subsp. pubescens, the North American subspecies of this same species rather than a separate species, and titles itself "Thelypteris palustris subsp. pubescens (Eastern Marsh Fern, Marsh Fern)", putting "Eastern Marsh Fern" ahead of "Marsh Fern". Because NC State's dedicated page is scoped to the subspecies rather than to the species as a whole, and RHS's dedicated page covers the exact species requested, "Marsh Fern" (RHS's lead name) was selected as common_name; "Eastern Marsh Fern" is a well-supported alternate primary name per NC State. NC State's Common Name(s) list carries the same two entries in the same order as the title, and its Description opens 'The eastern marsh fern is a native herbaceous perennial'; RHS's 'Other common names' list ('ground fern, marsh buckler fern') omits marsh fern, which the profile renders as the lead name beneath the botanical name. The catalog's first Thelypteris.
unknowns: No admissible source (NC State's dedicated Thelypteris palustris subsp. pubescens page, or RHS's Thelypteris palustris page) carries any toxicity, poison, or skin-irritation information for this species/taxon, scoped to cats, dogs, or otherwise -- toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are left null.

is_houseplant false rests on NC State's Plant Type field (Fern, Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant), its Landscape Location values (Naturalized Area, Pond, Riparian, Woodland) and RHS's Cultivation note; no admissible source frames this fern as an indoor/houseplant -- both dedicated pages describe only outdoor/garden landscape use.

No admissible source gives day/night temperature ranges, humidity percentages, light in foot-candles, a chill-damage onset temperature, a numeric water-check depth/interval, or fertilizer interval/strength for this species -- all left null.

soil_ph left null on both ends: NC State's Soil pH tag is the open-ended "Acid (<6.0)" band (no floor per the open-band rule), and RHS gives only the categorical tags "Neutral or Acid" with no numeric pH values to derive a ceiling from.

soil_drainage left null: admissible sources give differing, non-matching moisture descriptions -- NC State's structured Soil Drainage tags are "Moist, Occasionally Wet" (no accompanying good-drainage or occasionally-dry tag), while RHS's Moisture field reads "Moist but well-drained or Poorly-drained", spanning moderate to wet-leaning without clearly committing to either the moderate or moisture_retentive bucket as defined.

water_regime left null: neither dedicated page (NC State, RHS) contains a structured watering statement or moisture-schedule field distinct from the bare soil-moisture descriptors already used for soil_drainage.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light Requirements for this taxon list both Full sun and Partial Shade, but RHS's structured Position/Sun field for the exact species T. palustris lists only Partial shade. Because only two admissible dedicated pages exist for this plant and they disagree, full_sun was excluded and only part_shade (supported by both) was retained.

No admissible single-species dedicated page was found on hgic.clemson.edu, extension.umd.edu, extension.psu.edu, edis.ifas.ufl.edu, ask.ifas.ufl.edu, or plantfinder.mobot.org/missouribotanicalgarden.org for this species -- those domains either had no page for Thelypteris palustris or only multi-species list pages (e.g. UGA CAES Field Report's "Native Plants for Georgia Part II: Ferns", a multi-species publication), which were excluded per the single-species-page rule even though the UGA page contains species-specific marsh fern text.

NC State's dedicated page covers Thelypteris palustris subsp. pubescens, the North American subspecies of this same species rather than a separate species; its content was used where applicable to the species, and the subspecies scope is noted here.
chill_damage_f left null: RHS gives only a hardiness rating (H7), which per the schema rules is a zone/survival rating, not a stated damage-onset temperature.

records.name_note: Sources split on which common name leads. NC State Extension's dedicated single-species page for this exact species (plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/dryopteris-cristata/) lists 'Crested Woodfern' as the first entry of its rendered 'Common Name(s):' list (second entry 'Narrow Swamp Fern'), and its browser-tab title likewise reads 'Dryopteris cristata (Crested Woodfern, Narrow Swamp Fern)'; the page's rendered H1 is the botanical name 'Dryopteris cristata' alone. RHS's dedicated single-species page instead renders 'crested buckler fern' as its lead common name directly beneath the H1 (and in its page title, 'Dryopteris cristata | crested buckler fern'), and files 'crested wood fern' under a separate heading, 'Other common names', which carries that one entry only -- so 'crested wood fern' is not RHS's primary name. Per the tie-break rule (prefer the source whose title/H1/lead name or first common-name-list item carries the name), 'Crested Woodfern' (= Crested Wood Fern) is used here because it is the first item of NC State's common-name list, while RHS's own lead name is 'crested buckler fern.' Distinct from Dryopteris marginalis (Evergreen Wood Fern) and Dryopteris erythrosora (Autumn Fern), already in this catalog.
unknowns: is_houseplant false rests on NC State's Plant Type field (Fern, Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant), its USDA Plant Hardiness Zone range (3a-7b) and its Description's landscape-use sentence; neither admissible source (NC State, RHS) frames this species as an indoor/houseplant subject.

toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: no Poison, Problem-for-Cats, or Problem-for-Dogs module was found on the NC State page (the only admissible source with that kind of structured toxicity field for this genus), and RHS's page carries no toxicity field for this species either -- left null rather than guessed.

chill_damage_f / cool_rest_note: neither source states a numeric damage-onset temperature or a cool-rest/dormancy care instruction; NC State gives only a USDA hardiness zone range (3a-7b), which is a survival-zone rating, not a damage-onset figure, so not used.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, light_fc_good: this species is treated by both sources purely as an outdoor garden/wetland fern (hardiness zones, landscape uses, aspect) rather than with indoor day/night temperature, humidity percentage, or foot-candle light targets, so these are left null.

direct_sun_hours_max: NC State's Partial Shade tag carries an hour range (2-6 hours) only as part of its site-wide light-category legend, not as species-specific prose, so per rule this was not used to populate direct_sun_hours_max.

outdoor_sun_exposure: neither source's structured field supports full_sun or part_sun for this species -- NC State's Light field lists only Dappled Sunlight, Deep shade, and Partial Shade, and RHS's Position field lists only Full shade and Partial shade -- so those two values are omitted.

soil_drainage: left null because the two admissible sources genuinely disagree. NC State's own Soil Drainage field states 'Frequent Standing Water' and 'Occasionally Wet' (supporting moisture_retentive), while RHS's Cultivation text explicitly warns 'moist (but not waterlogged)', which per the same-source-warning rule overrides RHS's own Moisture field ('Moist but well-drained or Poorly-drained') toward a more moderate, non-waterlogged reading. The two sources' net positions conflict, so soil_drainage is left null.

soil_ph_min/max: NC State's pH field is the open-ended 'Acid (<6.0)' band, which per rule sets neither a floor nor a ceiling. RHS's pH field is only the categorical 'Neutral or Acid' with no numeric range given on the page, so no numeric bound could be derived from either source; left null.

water_regime / water_dry_down_target / water_check_depth_cm / water_growing_days_est / water_dormant_days_est / water_estimate_basis: neither source gives an explicit watering statement or structured moisture-schedule field (only habitat description and soil-drainage tags, which the rules exclude from water_regime); this is also an in-ground garden perennial, for which the day-interval and dry-down fields are to be left null absent a source that frames watering that way. All left null.
fertilize_interval_days / fertilize_active_months / fertilize_strength: no fertilizing guidance of any kind was found on either the NC State or RHS page for this species; left null.

common_name researched as 'Crested Wood Fern'; landed as 'Crested Woodfern', the one-word form NC State's Common Name(s) list and Description use, which keeps it distinct from Evergreen Wood Fern (Dryopteris marginalis) already in this catalog.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name leads. NC State's page title is 'Asplenium platyneuron (Brownstem Spleenwort, Ebony Spleenwort)' and its Common Name(s) field is a two-entry alphabetized list, Brownstem Spleenwort then Ebony Spleenwort, in the same order as the page-title parenthetical; NC State's own Description nonetheless opens 'Ebony Spleenwort is a diminutive evergreen fern in the Spleenwort family (Aspleniaceae).' Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated Plant Finder page carries a single Common Name value, 'ebony spleenwort', and its prose opens 'Asplenium platyneuron, commonly called ebony spleenwort'; RHS's dedicated species page leads with 'ebony spleenwort' in its page title and plant-profile subtitle, and its Other common names field carries that single value. All three dedicated pages lead with ebony spleenwort in their profile lead or opening prose, so common_name is 'Ebony Spleenwort'; Brownstem Spleenwort is NC State's alphabetically first list entry. Distinct from Asplenium nidus (Bird's Nest Fern), already in this catalog.
unknowns: is_houseplant false rests on NC State's Plant Type field (Fern, Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant), its USDA Plant Hardiness Zone range (3a-9b) and Landscape Theme value 'Shade Garden', and Missouri Botanical Garden's Uses sentence. None of the three admissible dedicated-species pages (NC State, Missouri Botanical Garden, RHS) frame this fern as an indoor/houseplant subject — all three treat it as an outdoor garden subject (Missouri Botanical Garden's Uses reads 'Plant in dryish, rocky, shady areas of rock gardens (will grow in rocky crevices), native plant gardens or woodland areas.'; RHS's suggested planting locations run from 'Rock garden' through 'Patio and container plants' to 'Flower borders and beds', i.e. outdoor containers rather than indoor culture).

toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: none of the admissible sources (NC State, Missouri Botanical Garden, RHS) mention toxicity, poison parts, or any hazard to cats, dogs, or any other animal for this species.

chill_damage_f left null: no admissible source states a numeric cold-damage-onset temperature. NC State gives only USDA hardiness zones (3a-9b) and RHS gives only its H5 hardiness rating (-15 to -10C, 'hardy in most places throughout the UK even in severe winters') — both regional/survival ratings, not damage-onset figures, per the rule against deriving chill damage from hardiness data.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min/good left null: no admissible source gives numeric temperature ranges, humidity percentages, or footcandle light levels for this species; all three are structured outdoor-garden plant profiles, not houseplant care datasheets.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: NC State's only hour figures ('Less than 2 hours', '2-6 hours') live inside its site-wide Light category legend (Deep shade / Partial Shade tag definitions), not in species-specific prose, so they are excluded per the rule against using NC State's generic light-category legend for this field.

soil_ph_min/max left null: NC State's Description prose states the species 'is not sensitive to pH but prefers acidic conditions with a pH of 4.5 to 5,' but RHS's structured pH field for this species reads 'Neutral or Alkaline or Acid,' explicitly listing alkaline soils as acceptable. Because RHS treats alkaline soil as tolerated while NC State's number is framed only as a preference (not a hard limit), both bounds are left null rather than asserting a ceiling or floor either source would contradict.

water_regime left null: Missouri Botanical Garden's structured Water field reads 'Dry to medium' and NC State's prose says 'dry to medium moisture' — both mid-scale structured/prose moisture readings that span dry-to-medium rather than clearly matching one of dry_surface_between/dry_thoroughly_between/keep_barely_moist/keep_moist, so the field is left null rather than forced into an enum value; Missouri Botanical Garden's Culture note also separately advises 'Avoid overwatering' and 'Needs excellent drainage to minimize risk of crown rot', and its Problems section adds that 'Crown rot can be a significant problem in poorly drained soils', consistent with a drier-leaning regime but not a specific watering instruction.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis left null: this is an in-ground garden/woodland fern, and no admissible source frames its watering in dry-down-target, check-depth, or day-interval terms.
fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, fertilize_strength left null: none of the admissible sources mention fertilizing this species at all.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes full_sun and part_sun: all three admissible structured sun fields cap exposure at partial shade or dimmer — NC State's Light field tops out at 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', Missouri Botanical Garden's Sun field reads 'Part shade to full shade', and RHS's Position field reads 'Partial shade'. NC State's Description prose does reach higher, saying the fern 'grows best in well-drained, rocky soils, in shade to part sun', but that prose bound is contradicted by NC State's own structured Light field and by both other sources, so part_sun is not asserted.

toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: neither RHS's nor MoBot's dedicated page states any toxicity, poisoning, or pet-safety information for this species.

chill_damage_f left null: RHS's H4 hardiness rating for this species page is a hardiness-zone survival rating (hardy through most of the UK, -10 to -5C), not a stated damage-onset temperature, so per rule it cannot be used to fill this field; MoBot's Zone 3 to 8 is likewise a hardiness-zone range, not an onset figure.

cool_rest_note, day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min/good, and direct_sun_hours_max all left null: no admissible source (RHS, MoBot) states numeric temperature, humidity, light-footcandle, or sun-hour figures for this species.

outdoor_sun_exposure includes only full_sun, supported by both RHS's structured Position field ("Full sun") and MoBot's structured Sun field ("Full sun to part shade"). part_shade is left out and disclosed here rather than included: MoBot's Sun field spans a range down to part shade, but RHS's structured Position field for this species lists only "Full sun", so the broader value is not corroborated across both admissible structured sun fields.

soil_base left null: none of the enum options (standard_potting, chunky_aroid, cactus_succulent, ericaceous, orchid_bark, african_violet, semi_hydro, garden_bed) accurately describes cultivation of an emergent aquatic sedge grown directly in saturated soil or standing pond/bog water, which is what both admissible sources describe (RHS: pond margins/bog gardens; MoBot: ponds, bogs, or shallow water up to 3 feet deep).

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, and fertilize_strength left null: neither RHS's nor MoBot's dedicated page for this species gives any fertilizing guidance.

records.name_note: Admissible sources split on which common name leads. NC State's dedicated Typha latifolia page carries a four-entry alphabetized Common Name(s) list ('Broadleaf Cattail', 'Bulrush', 'Cat-O'-Nine-Tails', 'Common Cattail'), Broadleaf Cattail first, while its Description opens 'The Common Cattail is a grass-like native plant to North Carolina.' Missouri Botanical Garden's dedicated page (kempercode a407) gives its Common Name field as 'broadleaf cattail' and its prose opens 'Typha latifolia, called common cattail'. RHS's dedicated page leads with a single common-name subtitle, 'bulrush', and carries a separate, longer Other common names list (asparagus of the Cossacks, baccobolts, blackcap, blackhead, bull segg, candlewick, cat o' nine tails, cat tail, cat's tail, dod, flax tail, great reedmace, March beetle, marsh beetle, marsh pestle, mat reed, nailrod, water torch) that does not include Broadleaf Cattail. Broadleaf Cattail is the landed name: it is the first entry of NC State's list and the value of MoBot's Common Name field, the structured lead on both North American dedicated pages; Common Cattail (both pages' prose) and bulrush (RHS) are disclosed as alternatives. The catalog's first Typha.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: no admissible source (NC State, RHS, or MoBot's dedicated Typha latifolia page, checked at landing) provides any toxicity information for this species, scoped to cats/dogs or otherwise. NC State's plant profile has no Poison section at all for this species, RHS's page has no toxicity field, and MoBot's page carries no toxicity statement. Left null rather than guessed.

chill_damage_f: RHS gives a bare hardiness rating of "H6" for this species (a survival/zone rating, tied to a site-wide legend of temperature bands, not a species-specific damage-onset figure), so per the rule against deriving chill damage from a hardiness rating, this was left null.

soil_ph_min / soil_ph_max: RHS's pH field for this species reads "Acid or Alkaline or Neutral" (all three, open-ended), so no ceiling or floor can be set from it. NC State's plant profile has no Soil pH field for this species at all. Left null.

soil_base: none of the enum options (standard_potting, chunky_aroid, cactus_succulent, ericaceous, orchid_bark, african_violet, semi_hydro, garden_bed) cleanly describes an emergent aquatic/wetland perennial whose NC State Landscape Location field renders four values — "Coastal", "Container", "Naturalized Area", "Pond" — and that RHS describes as planted in boggy soil or submerged pond margins. Rather than force a mismatched category, left null.

water_regime set to keep_moist as the closest available enum value, but both admissible sources actually describe standing/submerged water conditions wetter than typical "keep_moist" usage: RHS's Cultivation notes call for pond margins at up to 30cm water depth, and NC State's Description says to cover the plant with up to 30 inches of water in a container. No enum option exists for a submerged aquatic emergent.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm, water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis, and all fertilize_* fields: neither NC State nor RHS frames watering or fertilizing for this species as a dry-down schedule, a check-depth routine, a day-interval, or a fertilizer regimen (fertilizing is not mentioned by either source at all), so these were left null.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max, humidity_need, humidity_pct_min/max, light_fc_min, light_fc_good, direct_sun_hours_max: neither admissible source states numeric temperature, ambient-humidity, or footcandle targets for this outdoor wetland perennial. NC State's Light field carries only its generic site-wide hour-range legend text ("Full sun (6 or more hours...)", "Partial Shade (...2-6 hours)"), which per the sourcing rules cannot be used to populate direct_sun_hours_max. Left null.

outdoor_sun_exposure includes part_shade on NC State's structured Light field (Full sun, Partial Shade) and on NC State's own species prose, "They prefer full sun to partial shade.", corroborated by MoBot's structured Sun field 'Sun: Full sun to part shade'. RHS's Position card shows only a "Full sun" icon and does not carry a second sun value — non-corroboration rather than exclusion, since RHS renders a single sun icon as a matter of course.

Clemson HGIC (hgic.clemson.edu), UF/IFAS (edis.ifas.ufl.edu / ask.ifas.ufl.edu), Penn State Extension (extension.psu.edu), and UGA fieldreport (fieldreport.caes.uga.edu) were checked but no dedicated single-species Typha latifolia page could be located/confirmed on any of them during this research session; they were not used as sources for any field.

University of Maryland Extension (extension.umd.edu) has a page titled "Cattail" (extension.umd.edu/resource/cattail), but it covers cattails generically -- its opening reads "There are four different 1 species of cattail in the North America, and all are commonly found in wet or hydric soils." (the stray "1" is the page's own footnote marker) -- without identifying Typha latifolia specifically (the string 'latifolia' does not appear on the page), so it is a genus/multi-species page, not a dedicated single-species page, and was excluded per the single-species-page requirement.

Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder was reported unreachable for this species during research; the audit found a live dedicated Typha latifolia page (kempercode a407), and it was read in the Browser pane at landing. It is cited here for common_name ('Common Name: broadleaf cattail'), outdoor_sun_exposure ('Sun: Full sun to part shade'), water_regime and soil_drainage ('Water: Wet'; Culture 'Easily grown in rich loams in full sun to part shade in water to 12” deep.'). It carries no toxicity statement. Its full common-name list lives only in an overlib tooltip attribute and is not quoted.

Spread and containment statements, captured as stated: NC State -- 'Grow in containers to control the spread in smaller ponds or water gardens and cover with up to 30 inches of water.' and, under Insects, Diseases and Other Plant Problems, 'Can become invasive.'; RHS Cultivation -- 'Root system may puncture pond liners, and in shallower water may spread rapidly, with potential to become a nuisance if not managed well.'; MoBot Culture -- 'Cattails are aggressive colonizers that if left unrestrained will crowd out most other marginal plants. Plant in containers or tubs to restrain spread.' and Problems 'Aggressive spreader outside of containers.' No schema field holds these, so they are recorded here.

normalizations: 2026-09-10: b77 landed by a second session (branch claude/database-build-goals-e548af) from the loop's post-audit records. Seven native wetland ferns and emergents land: Royal Fern, Netted Chain Fern, Marsh Fern, Crested Woodfern, Ebony Spleenwort, Common Spike-rush, Broadleaf Cattail. Auditor's corrected wording used verbatim; every substitute quote ground-truthed with qc.py, or read off the rendered MoBot page in the Browser pane where MoBot refuses this machine's fetcher. Landing decisions: Osmunda regalis drops full_sun (MoBot's structured Sun field excludes it and its Culture text recommends against it; NC State and RHS carry full sun only behind a cool-summer / constant-moisture condition); Woodwardia areolata's soil_drainage restored to moisture_retentive on the audit's reasoning (the null rested on UGA's Habitat field read as a cultivation range; NC State's structured Soil Drainage field is Frequent Standing Water / Moist / Occasionally Wet and MoBot states 'Needs consistently moist soils.'); MoBot pages the researcher reported unreachable (Woodwardia areolata v200, Typha latifolia a407) cited after a landing re-check; NC State label-glued and space-joined quotes re-quoted as newline-stacked values with Landscape Location and Landscape Theme split; Dryopteris cristata lands as Crested Woodfern, NC State's one-word list lead, distinct from Evergreen Wood Fern (D. marginalis). Sparganium americanum is WITHHELD from this batch: no admissible domain carries a dedicated single-species page (NC State 404, RHS has no S. americanum entry, MoBot none, and nothing on Clemson, UF/IFAS EDIS/ask, Penn State, UMD or UGA), so its record has zero citations and an unsupported common_name that the loader would refuse; it is a coverage gap, not a naming conflict. verify_quotes: every reachable quote verified after repair; MoBot pages skipped from this machine.
